results.api: ws.RelayConnect + Client.Subscribe (Events / EndOfStoredEvents channels)
results.crypto: orly's in-tree p256k1 (mleku's p256k1.mleku.dev: pure Go + amd64 assembly)
results.notes: Verification is the library's default (Client.AssumeValid=false): event.E.Verify checks the signature against the id as received and recomputes the id only when the signature fails, so the harness also compares the library's GetIDBytes() (canonical hash) with the id of every delivered event. That comparison cannot catch everything: when the signature fails, Verify recomputes the id, OVERWRITES ev.ID with it and accepts the event if the signature is valid for the computed id (orly pkg/nostr/encoders/event/verify.go:23-34; ws.Client only looks at the bool), so an event with a wrong id field but a signature over its true id is delivered under the corrected id and the harness's check passes (no corpus event is of that shape; the accepted XOR would show it). Its JSON decoder keeps \uXXXX escapes verbatim in content and tags (a corpus event whose content holds \uD83D\uDE44 is delivered with those 12 characters, not the emoji), so for the ~2,400 events sent with escaped emoji the canonical hash does not match the id and the harness drops them; without that id check the library would deliver them, with their text mangled. lol log level set to "off" (default "info" prints one stderr line per rejected event). JSON: the library's own envelope and event decoders (binary id/pubkey/sig fields)

results.api: client.Connect + Connection.Subscribe (typed events channel, closed at EOSE)
results.crypto: flokicoin crypto/schnorr v0.25.12-alpha (btcec fork) on dcrd secp256k1/v4 v4.4.0 (pure Go)
results.notes: Diagnostic: the common path its docs give. Its read loop also pushes every message onto the connection's shared incoming channel (buffer 10240), which nobody reads in this style (its docs say not to mix it with Read()), so after 10240 messages the read loop blocks for good and EOSE never arrives. The client delivers events unverified; the harness calls nip01.Event.Verify(nip01.WithoutPowCheck()) (format, id recomputed and compared, BIP-340 signature) on each; WithoutPowCheck turns off the NIP-13 proof-of-work check Verify otherwise runs (a second id hash) on events with a nonce tag, work outside the job. The harness drains Connection.Errors() (unbuffered; the read loop blocks on it otherwise). EOSE = the events channel closing. JSON: encoding/json (Conn.ReadJSON)
results.error: run 1: timeout: no EOSE within 5m0s (9049 events delivered)

results.crypto: flokicoin crypto/schnorr v0.25.12-alpha (btcec fork) on dcrd secp256k1/v4 v4.4.0 (pure Go)

The connection's read loop blocks on an unbuffered Errors() channel, so the harness drains it. JSON: encoding/json (Conn.ReadJSON)

results.api: client.NewRelayManager + Connect + Subscribe + Subscription.Receive (callback) / EOSE() channel
results.crypto: btcec/v2 v2.3.6 on dcrd secp256k1/v4 v4.4.0 (pure Go)
results.notes: R&D-stage library. Its read loop hands each event to the subscription with a non-blocking send on an unbuffered channel, so every event that arrives while the app is still busy with the previous one is dropped: it delivers a different, small subset on every run. The client delivers events unverified; the harness calls Event.ValidateSignature() (signature over sha256(Serialize()), id field not compared) and compares sha256(Serialize()) with the id on each. JSON: encoding/json envelope + easyjson event decoder

Verification is the library's default (RelayOptions.AssumeValid=false): VerifySignature recomputes the id into a copy of the event and verifies the signature against it, never comparing it with the id field, so the harness also calls the library's Event.CheckID() on every delivered event. SubscriptionOptions.MaxWaitForEOSE is disabled (math.MaxInt64): its 7 s default dispatches a fake EOSE and drops the stored events still queued. InfoLogger (stderr by default, one line per rejected event) is sent to io.Discard. JSON: gjson envelope split + easyjson event decoder

results.api: ws.RelayConnect + Client.Subscribe (Events / EndOfStoredEvents channels)
results.crypto: orly's in-tree p256k1 (mleku's p256k1.mleku.dev: pure Go + amd64 assembly)
results.notes: Verification is the library's default (Client.AssumeValid=false): event.E.Verify checks the signature against the id as received and recomputes the id only when the signature fails, so the harness also compares the library's GetIDBytes() (canonical hash) with the id of every delivered event. That comparison cannot catch everything: when the signature fails, Verify recomputes the id, OVERWRITES ev.ID with it and accepts the event if the signature is valid for the computed id (orly pkg/nostr/encoders/event/verify.go:23-34; ws.Client only looks at the bool), so an event with a wrong id field but a signature over its true id is delivered under the corrected id and the harness's check passes (no corpus event is of that shape; the accepted XOR would show it). Its JSON decoder keeps \uXXXX escapes verbatim in content and tags (a corpus event whose content holds \uD83D\uDE44 is delivered with those 12 characters, not the emoji), so for the ~2,400 events sent with escaped emoji the canonical hash does not match the id and the harness drops them; without that id check the library would deliver them, with their text mangled. lol log level set to "off" (default "info" prints one stderr line per rejected event). JSON: the library's own envelope and event decoders (binary id/pubkey/sig fields)

results.api: client.Connect + Connection.Subscribe (typed events channel, closed at EOSE)
results.crypto: flokicoin crypto/schnorr v0.25.12-alpha (btcec fork) on dcrd secp256k1/v4 v4.4.0 (pure Go)
results.notes: Diagnostic: the common path its docs give. Its read loop also pushes every message onto the connection's shared incoming channel (buffer 10240), which nobody reads in this style (its docs say not to mix it with Read()), so after 10240 messages the read loop blocks for good and EOSE never arrives. The client delivers events unverified; the harness calls nip01.Event.Verify(nip01.WithoutPowCheck()) (format, id recomputed and compared, BIP-340 signature) on each; WithoutPowCheck turns off the NIP-13 proof-of-work check Verify otherwise runs (a second id hash) on events with a nonce tag, work outside the job. The harness drains Connection.Errors() (unbuffered; the read loop blocks on it otherwise). EOSE = the events channel closing. JSON: encoding/json (Conn.ReadJSON)

results.api: client.NewRelayManager + Connect + Subscribe + Subscription.Receive (callback) / EOSE() channel
results.crypto: btcec/v2 v2.3.6 on dcrd secp256k1/v4 v4.4.0 (pure Go)
results.notes: R&D-stage library. Its read loop hands each event to the subscription with a non-blocking send on an unbuffered channel, so every event that arrives while the app is still busy with the previous one is dropped: it delivers a different, small subset on every run. The client delivers events unverified; the harness calls Event.ValidateSignature() (signature over sha256(Serialize()), id field not compared) and compares sha256(Serialize()) with the id on each. JSON: encoding/json envelope + easyjson event decoder
